text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Liberal popularity still strong, poll says: Stirrings of support for Tories, NDP not enough yet to hurt dominance outside Quebec.
- Inuit leaders give invitation to separatists: Sovereigntists challenged to describe vision for Quebec to northern people.
- Chretien adjusts warmth dial: links good, 'not cozy.'
- Serbian opposition faces denuded cities: Mayors tackle debt, empty treasuries.
- Ontario's topless issue looms large over summer: Worried town councils are consulting lawyers to see where they stand, should half-clad women take to the pools.
- Busang tampering challenged: Bre-X's detail on assays by Indonesian company suggests any salting not done in field.
- D-day for Bre-X is April 29: That's day triple-checking of results to come in, official says.
- K mart reassures suppliers they won't be 'disadvantaged': Retailer reacts to vendors' nervousness.
- Talisman kills Wascana bid: Clears way for CanOxy's friendly C$1.9-billion bid.
- Nortel in C$1-billion selloff: Major change of business focus leads telecom giant to shed control of its North American equipment distribution business.
- Canadian 88 on the block after losing out on Morrison.
